kf: Crops of 1–5 mm **yellow papules with a red halo** on buttocks, extensor limbs and shoulders.
Marker of **severe hypertriglyceridaemia** (usually TG over 10–20 mmol/L).
Common drivers: **uncontrolled diabetes**, obesity, alcohol, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, drugs (oestrogens, retinoids, antipsychotics, steroids).
Risk of **acute pancreatitis**: check glucose, HbA1c, fasting lipids, TFT, U&E, LFT, urine protein.
Treat the cause; papules fade over weeks as triglycerides fall.
myths: **"They're just spots"**: they mean dangerously high triglycerides.
patho_lead: Lipid **leaks from blood into the dermis** and macrophages eat it.

mech.t: Lipoprotein lipase activity falls (e.g. insulin deficiency); triglyceride-rich particles build up.
Macrophages take up the lipid and become foam cells.
mech.cap: Lipid particles leave dermal capillaries and are engulfed by macrophages, forming foam cells.

prog: Papules clear within weeks to months of control.
